checks: Compared frozen proof to original bd886f63d6450164 through its proof before Conditional application. The fixed sign, continuous positive weight, distributional curvature support and nondegenerate coefficient hypotheses are all explicit.

For two zeros separated by a positive point, verified the two mean-value steps. Endpoint derivatives are zero, then the ordered second-derivative signs are positive, negative, positive. Positive w transfers these signs to the load.

Concavity forbids that first triple, while convexity forbids the negative, positive, negative subsequence produced from two such gaps. This bounds the number of connected zero components without assuming any a priori finiteness of zeros.

When a zero component is an interval, H'' vanishes there. A convex load vanishing on an interval is nonnegative on both exterior sides, so H is convex and its zero set is connected. The concave case gives H concave and an interior nonnegative zero forces H identically zero. In either case a nonzero arm coefficient makes A affine on the zero interval, so only endpoints can carry curvature. An affine nonzero load cannot vanish on an interval.

Checked the empty-zero and identically-zero H cases and that endpoints of the open domain are excluded by the statement. The result has conditional contact hypotheses and makes no general multiplier or profile extremizer assertion.

overlap.comparison: This is a sampled nonnegative concave-sequence moment inequality. Its hypotheses contain neither a signed second-derivative potential nor a support relation, and it gives no continuum curvature-support conclusion.

readability: The convex versus concave sign obstruction is clear after placing the two possible gaps in their order on the interval.
